section: Peshwas and the Maratha confederacy; Third Battle of Panipat (1761); three Anglo-Maratha wars
subsections: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: The Mughal grant secured through the Sayyids in 1719 recognised which of the following for Shahu?
o: The right to appoint the Mughal emperor
Exclusive control over Punjab and Gujarat
Only the right to collect land revenue in Malwa
Swarajya along with chauth and sardeshmukhi of the Deccan
accepted.x: Balaji Vishwanath obtained the 1719 Mughal grant recognising Shahu’s swarajya and granting the Marathas the right to collect chauth and sardeshmukhi in the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Split the option by checking the complete bundle of rights rather than accepting a partial match.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Baji Rao I:
1. He won Malwa and Bundelkhand.
2. He raided Delhi in 1737.
3. He organised the Maratha confederacy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Baji Rao I won Malwa and Bundelkhand, raided Delhi in 1737 and is associated with organising the Maratha confederacy.
accepted.tq: Check each contribution separately before selecting the inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: The Battle of Palkhed, fought in 1728, was associated with which Peshwa?
accepted.x: Baji Rao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed in 1728; the subsequent settlement is also referred to as the Treaty of Palkhed.
accepted.tq: Match the battle with the correct Peshwa instead of confusing the battle with a later Maratha–Nizam conflict.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Balaji Baji Rao, also known as Nana Saheb?
o: He was the infant Peshwa confirmed by the Treaty of Salbai.
He presided over the zenith of Maratha power and reached Lahore and Peshawar.
He was the Peshwa who organised the confederacy after the Battle of Palkhed.
accepted.x: Balaji Baji Rao, or Nana Saheb, was Peshwa from 1740 to 1761, during which Maratha power reached its zenith and Maratha forces reached Lahore and Peshawar.
accepted.tq: Use the exact title–person association and eliminate options belonging to other Peshwas.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the achievement of Madhav Rao I after 1761?
o: He signed the Treaty of Bassein and became the last Peshwa.
He revived Maratha power after Panipat and defeated several regional opponents.
He founded Peshwa power and secured the 1719 Mughal grant.
He was removed by the Barabhai council immediately after his accession.
accepted.x: Madhav Rao I revived Maratha power after Panipat and defeated the Nizam, Mysore under Haidar Ali, Rohillas, Rajputs and Jats.
accepted.tq: Identify the recovery phase and reject contributions belonging to earlier or later Peshwas.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Madhav Rao I defeated Haidar Ali of Mysore.
2. Madhav Rao I defeated the Rohillas, Rajputs and Jats.
3. Mahadji Scindia restored Shah Alam II to Delhi in 1771.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Madhav Rao I defeated the listed regional powers, while Mahadji Scindia restored Shah Alam II to Delhi in 1771.
accepted.tq: Group closely related achievements, while checking whether the dated restoration belongs to the same phase.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Narayan Rao was killed in a succession struggle with whom?
accepted.x: Narayan Rao was murdered in 1773 during a succession feud involving his uncle, Raghunath Rao.
accepted.tq: Use the kinship relationship to avoid confusing the rival Peshwa with the later Barabhai leader.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which body ousted Raghunath Rao from the position of Peshwa?
accepted.x: Raghunath Rao, also called Raghoba, was ousted by the Barabhai council in 1774.
accepted.tq: Apply the institution–action pairing and reject historically prominent but unrelated bodies.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Raghunath Rao’s attempt to obtain British assistance became associated with which conflict?
accepted.x: Raghunath Rao sought British help, and this intervention led to the First Anglo-Maratha War.
accepted.tq: Link the individual claimant to the war triggered by his appeal for outside support.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Madhav Rao II was best described as which of the following?
o: An infant Peshwa who ruled through Nana Phadnavis
The Peshwa who secured the 1719 grant from the Mughals
The last Peshwa who signed the Treaty of Bassein
The Peshwa who raided Delhi in 1737
accepted.x: Madhav Rao II became Peshwa as an infant and governed through Nana Phadnavis.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive age and regency clue to distinguish Madhav Rao II from other Peshwas.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: What was the relationship between the Treaty of Salbai and Madhav Rao II?
o: The treaty recognised or confirmed him after his installation as an infant.
The treaty installed him as Peshwa in 1774.
The treaty removed him from the Peshwa office.
The treaty was signed by him as the last Peshwa in 1818.
accepted.x: Madhav Rao II had already been installed as an infant in 1774; the Treaty of Salbai later recognised or confirmed his position.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of installation from the later treaty that recognised the infant Peshwa.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: The defeat of the Nizam at Kharda in 1795 took place during the tenure of which Peshwa?
accepted.x: Madhav Rao II was the Peshwa during the Maratha victory over the Nizam at Kharda in 1795.
accepted.tq: Match the battle and year with the correct later Peshwa.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Baji Rao II — Treaty of Bassein, 1802
Madhav Rao I — Treaty of Bassein, 1802
accepted.x: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein in 1802. He was the last Peshwa and was later deposed and pensioned.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure treaty–Peshwa pair and eliminate the swapped office-holders.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Baji Rao II is correct?
o: He was the founder of effective Peshwa power.
He was the infant Peshwa confirmed by the Treaty of Salbai.
He was the Peshwa who defeated the Nizam at Palkhed.
He was the last Peshwa, and the office was abolished after his deposition.
accepted.x: Baji Rao II was the last Peshwa. He was deposed and pensioned, after which the office of Peshwa was abolished.
accepted.tq: Use the final-holder clue and distinguish it from the infant Peshwa Madhav Rao II.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the names of the Peshwas?
o: Balaji Baji Rao was also known as Nana Saheb.
Balaji Vishwanath was also known as Nana Saheb.
Madhav Rao I was also known as Nana Saheb.
Raghunath Rao was also known as Nana Saheb.
accepted.x: Nana Saheb refers to Balaji Baji Rao, not Balaji Vishwanath.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar names by linking the popular title to the correct Balaji.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Raghunath Rao was the uncle of which Peshwa?
accepted.x: Raghunath Rao was the uncle of Madhav Rao I; he should not be described as Madhav Rao I’s younger brother.
accepted.tq: Check the exact family relationship instead of accepting a close but incorrect kinship description.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Peshwas in chronological order of their tenure:
A. Madhav Rao II
B. Balaji Vishwanath
C. Baji Rao II
D. Narayan Rao
accepted.x: The correct order is Balaji Vishwanath, Narayan Rao, Madhav Rao II and Baji Rao II.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest Peshwas first, then place the two eighteenth-century successors between them.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Madhav Rao I held office from 1761 to 1772. The tenure 1772–1773 belongs to Narayan Rao.
accepted.tq: Find the one tenure that belongs to a neighbouring Peshwa rather than the named person.
accepted.sec: Peshwas → chronological order, key contribution, conquests and treaties

accepted.s: Who commanded the Maratha forces at the Third Battle of Panipat?
accepted.x: Sadashiv Rao Bhau was the principal commander of the Maratha forces. Vishwas Rao, the Peshwa’s son, also fought and was killed in the battle.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the field commander from the Peshwa and his son.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Maratha side at Panipat is correct?
1. Vishwas Rao was the son of the Peshwa.
2. Sadashiv Rao Bhau and Vishwas Rao were killed in the battle.
3. Ibrahim Khan Gardi commanded the Maratha artillery.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Vishwas Rao was Balaji Baji Rao’s son, Sadashiv Rao Bhau and Vishwas Rao were killed, and Ibrahim Khan Gardi led the artillery.
accepted.tq: Separate command, family and casualty details before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Who was the Peshwa at the time of the Third Battle of Panipat?
accepted.x: Balaji Baji Rao, popularly known as Nana Saheb, was the Peshwa when the Third Battle of Panipat was fought.
accepted.tq: Match the major event with the contemporary office-holder, not the battlefield commander.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Who was the Mughal emperor at the time of the Third Battle of Panipat?
accepted.x: Shah Alam II was the Mughal emperor during the Third Battle of Panipat.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological position of the Mughal emperor to avoid swapping him with earlier and later rulers.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: What was the immediate motive that led Ahmad Shah Abdali to intervene against the Marathas in North India?
o: The Marathas had expelled Timur Shah from Punjab.
The Marathas had defeated Shuja-ud-Daula in Awadh.
The Marathas had occupied Bengal after Plassey.
The Marathas had abolished the Mughal emperor’s office.
accepted.x: The Marathas drove Abdali’s son Timur Shah out of Punjab, including Lahore, in 1758, threatening Abdali’s influence in the region.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate trigger rather than a later consequence of the battle.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly explains the Maratha advance that alarmed Ahmad Shah Abdali?
o: Balaji Vishwanath reached Lahore and Attock in 1719.
Madhav Rao I reached Lahore and Attock after 1761.
Baji Rao II reached Lahore and Attock in 1802.
Raghunath Rao reached Lahore and Attock in 1758.
accepted.x: Raghunath Rao’s advance to Lahore and Attock in 1758 threatened Abdali’s hold over Punjab and contributed to the conflict.
accepted.tq: Match the northern advance with its correct leader and year.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consisted of important allies of Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat?
o: Suraj Mal and the Rajput chiefs
accepted.x: Abdali was supported by the Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh.
accepted.tq: Match the allied leaders with the correct side instead of assuming that all North Indian chiefs supported the Marathas.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Who invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to intervene against the Marathas?
accepted.x: Najib-ud-Daula, the Rohilla chief, invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to intervene against the Maratha expansion in North India.
accepted.tq: Identify the initiator of the intervention rather than confusing him with an ally of the opposing side.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Maratha position before the Third Battle of Panipat:
1. The Jats under Suraj Mal stayed away from the conflict.
2. The Rajputs also stayed away from the Maratha side.
3. The Marathas had extensive support from the major northern powers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Jats under Suraj Mal and the Rajputs stayed away, so the Marathas lacked substantial northern support. Statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in the third statement and retain the two statements describing absence of allies.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a major cause of the Maratha defeat at Panipat?
o: Alienation of some regional powers through earlier plunder
Heavy baggage and the presence of non-combatants
Strong and sustained support from the Jats and Rajputs
Collapse of supplies and starvation in the camp
accepted.x: The Marathas did not receive strong support from the Jats and Rajputs; their absence or neutrality contributed to the defeat. Supply failure, heavy baggage and alienation of regional powers were among the causes.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented condition of the Maratha alliance system.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Who recorded an eyewitness account of the Third Battle of Panipat while serving Shuja-ud-Daula?
accepted.x: Kashiraj Pandit was an eyewitness chronicler who served Shuja-ud-Daula and recorded an account of the battle.
accepted.tq: Match the chronicler with his patron and distinguish him from military commanders.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best describes the immediate political consequence of the Third Battle of Panipat?
o: Maratha power was permanently destroyed throughout India.
The Mughal Empire immediately regained effective control over all India.
Maratha ambitions in North India were halted, but Maratha power later recovered.
The East India Company was expelled from Bengal and the Carnatic.
accepted.x: The battle halted Maratha imperial ambitions in the north and caused heavy losses, but Maratha power was not destroyed and recovered within about a decade.
accepted.tq: Avoid the extreme-word trap in the claim of permanent destruction and focus on the qualified consequence.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which of the following developments contributed to the weakening of Peshwa control over the Maratha chiefs?
o: The victory of Baji Rao I at Palkhed in 1728
The death of Madhav Rao I in 1772
The occupation of Gujarat under Balaji Baji Rao
accepted.x: Peshwa control over the chiefs weakened especially after the death of Madhav Rao I in 1772.
accepted.tq: Connect the institutional consequence with the correct later turning point.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: The political vacuum following the weakening of Maratha power helped which power expand, particularly after its victories at Plassey and Wandiwash?
accepted.x: The political vacuum helped the East India Company, which had already won Plassey in 1757 and Wandiwash in 1760.
accepted.tq: Link the consequence to the power whose earlier military victories are specified.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Balaji Baji Rao after the Third Battle of Panipat?
o: He restored Shah Alam II to Delhi in 1771.
He became the Mughal emperor after the battle.
He became the commander of Abdali’s artillery.
accepted.x: Balaji Baji Rao died soon after the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.
accepted.tq: Separate the Peshwa’s post-battle fate from the later restoration carried out by Mahadji Scindia.
accepted.sec: Third Battle of Panipat (1761)
